Commentary.Commentary: We're back. Some words of motivation are delivered to the Zimbabwean players before they take the field. The clouds have been blown away, stiff breeze there, and the sun is out as well. Joe Moores and Ben Dawkins are the English openers. Two slips in place. Shelton Mazvitorera is ready to bowl with the first new ball. Let's play...
... CHASE TIME ...

So then, in the last game, England's batting did not quite hit its stride and they were restricted to 210 by Pakistan. The target today is not far off, and the conditions feel spicier. All signs point towards an intriguing second essay. Do Zimbabwe have the quality in their bowling ranks? Do they have the discipline, and more importantly, the fight? We will find out very soon.

The star pacer says that this is a pretty difficult ground for the seamers due to the stiff breeze and also, with one side being very short. On his 3 scalps, Manny says that he started a touch short in his opening spell but was beating the bat a lot. So he believed in himself and came back later to pick up wickets. Adds that he will take this confidence into future games. On the chats with his skipper, ML says that the conversation was pretty clear, on the lines and plans and what the team is trying to achieve. Details that the plan was to keep the line around the stumps and just keep it simple.

As mentioned, the entire English bowling group put in an impressive shift. Apart from Minto, everyone got among the wickets. The two spinners, Ralphie Albert and Farhan Ahmed, did the damage through the middle overs, combining for four wickets, while Manny Lumsden led the way with three scalps to finish as the standout bowler. Here he is for a quick chat...

Keeping the opposition to a modest total is usually reason enough to smile, and England will do so. Yet, somewhere deep down, there may be a bruised ego. With so much quality at their disposal and conditions tailor-made for seam bowling, they would have wanted to dominate Zimbabwe more. They were disciplined, kept the runs in check, fielded neatly and never allowed momentum to build. But bowling the hosts out much earlier would have been the ideal outcome. England will be satisfied, but perhaps not completely.

Was there nothing worth talking about in Zimbabwe's batting? Not quite, and that is what makes it more disappointing. Kian Blignaut and his partnership with Dhruv Patel were a joy to watch, especially with both the balls still fairly new. The letdown was that neither went on to make it count. Tatenda Chimugoro showed he can handle both pace and spin, and his three hefty blows hinted at real quality, but his stay was short and the impact limited. The skipper, Simbarashe Mudzengerere, was the one who truly dug in. With no disrespect to him, he may not have looked the most polished, but his resolve and willingness to occupy the crease stood out. He finished unbeaten on 45 off 63 balls, a knock that won't make it to the highlight reels but is important enough to give the home team a score above 200. One cannot forget his 40-run stand with Leeroy Chiwaula off 46 balls, and that was the only moment they looked in a bit of control.

It was a fairly underwhelming batting display from Zimbabwe. Yes, they have managed to bat through the full 50 overs against a quality England attack, and that does count for something. But it never quite felt like a performance targeted towards winning the game. In modern cricket, that might look more like an exercise for survival.
It is some sort of achievement for the Zimbabwe Under-19s that they were not bowled out. A small win, perhaps, but one they will quietly take.

In the sport. Terrific keeping. Beautifully tossed up, by Farhan Ahmed, keeping it very slow, making the ball to dip, Brendon Senzere lunges to defend but is beaten by the lack of pace. The ball lands and goes past the outside edge. Because of the lunge, Senzere's back foot rises ever so slightly but that is enough for Rew. Collects the ball and even before we could say 'GO!', the bails were dislodged. He knew it straightaway and started to celebrate but then realized that an appeal had to be made for stumping. It was referred upstairs and the replays showed that before the back foot could get down, the bails were off. Commentary.Commentary: Conditions are overcast, though there is no immediate threat of rain. It should offer some movement for the bowlers, and the English attack will be licking its lips, keen to make early inroads. Nathaniel Hlabangana and Kupakwashe Muradzi are the openers for Zimbabwe. Alex French to take the first new ball. Two slips in place. Here we go...

Pitch report - Natasha Farrant reckons the outfield will be a touch quicker today as the groundsmen have cut the grass. Andy Flower also, near the surface, points out that the pitch has a clear two-tone look. Adds that one end has a fair bit of grass, the other is patchy and dry. The Zimbabwean legend feels that if the ball lands in that drier area, it could skid on and stay low, keeping batters on their toes.
The national anthems of both teams are being played at the ground with the players lined up. England's anthem first, followed by the anthem of the co-host, Zimbabwe.

Zimbabwe Under-19 (Playing XI) - Nathaniel Hlabangana, Kupakwashe Muradzi (WK), Benny Zuze, Kian Blignaut, Leeroy Chiwaula, Brendon Senzere, Michael Blignaut, Simbarashe Mudzengerere (C), Dhruv Patel, Tatenda Chimugoro and Shelton Mazvitorera.

England Under-19 (Playing XI) - Ben Dawkins, Joe Moores, Ben Mayes, Thomas Rew (C) (WK), Caleb Falconer, Ralphie Albert, Farhan Ahmed, Luke Hands (In for Sebastian Morgan), James Minto, Manny Lumsden and Alex French (In for Alex Green).

The captain of Zimbabwe, Simbarashe Mudzengerere, says he would have bowled first as well, feeling it is a good wicket and that is the right way to go. Tells that the afternoon conditions might suit the bowlers, with the surface a bit up and down and potentially tough for batting. He adds that the key is to stay positive.

The skipper of England, Thomas Rew, says the wicket is fresh and has been under covers, so there could be something in it early on for the pacers. He feels the bowling display against Pakistan was special and adds that the side is looking to bat a bit deeper this time. He notes that the pitch has been uneven with a slow outfield, but says they have learnt a lot from the previous game. Rew adds that the plan is to go hard from ball one and set the tone early, and he confirms that there are two changes in the XI - Alex French and Luke Hands come in.
Toss - Both captains, Thomas Rew and Simbarashe Mudzengerere, ​​​​​​are in the middle for the coin toss. The former calls it correcly and England Under-19 elect to bowl!

After brushing past New Zealand and India in the warm-ups and then edging out Pakistan in the tournament proper, England have made a strong early statement. It is a quality squad, clearly motivated, and with an eye on lifting the trophy for the first time since 1997/98. The win over Pakistan also offered a few useful lessons. Even in victory, there were areas to sharpen. Conditions are expected to be similar again, and while Zimbabwe may not possess the same bowling depth as Pakistan, England will want to be smarter through the middle overs when the ball loses its shine. A statement win is firmly on the agenda. How convincingly they deliver it is the question. Stay tuned for toss and other updates...

Zimbabwe did get a couple of warm-up games under their belt, although the bowling did look a touch light in patches. With the bat too, one of the outings left a lot to be desired. Still, this is a group of handy young cricketers, and on home soil, you would expect a bit more bite and belief. That said, running into a well-oiled outfit like England is never a gentle introduction. It is the kind of contest that puts class, skill and temperament under the spotlight.

Hello, everyone! It is finally time for the home side, Zimbabwe, to get their Under-19 World Cup 2026 campaign rolling after their opening match against Scotland was washed away. The weather has been playing spoilsport in this part of the world, and the hosts will be hoping the skies show a bit of mercy today. Standing in their way are England, coming off a good win over Pakistan and keen to surf that winning wave a little longer. For Zimbabwe, it is a fresh start. For England, it is a chance to keep the momentum ticking along.

The stage is set for a high-octane encounter in Match 10 of the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2026 as the Young Lions of England face off against the tournament's co-hosts, Zimbabwe. Taking place at the historic Takashinga Sports Club in Harare, this Group C clash is more than just a game, it is a battle for dominance and a critical step toward the Super Six stage. Led by Somerset’s talented wicketkeeper-batter Thomas Rew, England enters this tournament with a point to prove. After a challenging tour of the West Indies late last year, the squad has been bolstered by the return of Rew and the rising form of Hampshire’s Ben Mayes. The Young Lions are hunting for their first U19 title since 1998. Their strength lies in a balanced bowling attack featuring Manny Lumsden, who has already made waves in the English domestic One Day Cup, and the tactical spin of vice-captain Farhan Ahmed. Playing on home soil, Zimbabwe is captained by Simbarashe Mudzengerere. The 'Chello' (as the locals call the youth side) are looking to leverage their familiarity with the Harare conditions to pull off an upset. All eyes will be on the Blignaut twins, Kian and Michael, sons of former Zimbabwe international Andy Blignaut. Kian Blignaut has been in sensational form leading up to the tournament, recently scoring a century in provincial games against senior professionals. His ability to anchor the innings will be vital against England’s pace battery. While England enters as favorites on paper due to their professional experience in the county circuit, Zimbabwe's home advantage and the recent form of their top order make them a dangerous underdog. A win here for either side almost guarantees a spot in the Super Sixes, making this one of the most pivotal fixtures of the opening week. Who are you backing for the win?
